title: How to build an AI clone of yourself that works 24/7

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: What if we could clone our own consciousness to work around the clock? How would that reshape our world?

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: We can now create AI clones using large language models and neural networks trained on personal data, but they lack true self-awareness.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: This raises concerns about identity, consent, and the potential for misuse if clones are used without ethical oversight.

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Builders are focusing on transparency, consent protocols, and watermarking AI outputs to distinguish them from human work.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: In the future, AI clones could assist in healthcare, education, and research, expanding human potential responsibly.

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: The future will balance innovation with ethics, ensuring AI clones enhance—not replace—our humanity.

video_cue: A person interacting with a holographic AI clone in a futuristic office setting.
